title: Coca-Cola's 2026 holiday campaign is made without generative AI
dek: After two years of AI-made holiday ads that drew public criticism, the company has put out human-made spots. Marketing Dive reports it is a deliberate change.
what: Marketing Dive reported on 19 November 2026 that Coca-Cola's holiday campaign, called "Enjoy Joy," does not use generative AI. It says this departs from the company's two earlier holiday campaigns, which did use it.

The spots were directed by Paul Dektor and show families and friends at football and shared meals, per the same report. Stacy Jackson, a vice president for the Coca-Cola trademark, is quoted: "There's something special about the role Coca-Cola plays during the holidays." She does not say in that quote that AI was dropped.

Marketing Dive says the earlier AI campaigns were divisive with consumers but beat the company's own performance targets. I did not find Coca-Cola saying why it changed course, so the reason is not established.
The post carrying the story is a 29-second video from an account that shares viral clips. I could not tell from the post which ad it shows.
why: The earlier AI ads were criticised widely, so a return to human-made work reads as a reaction to that, though Coca-Cola has not said so. Brands and viewers are watching how AI is used in advertising.
next: Whether Coca-Cola says anything further about its use of AI in future campaigns.

sources.label: Marketing Dive: Coca-Cola pivots from divisive AI-generated ads for holiday campaign (19 November)
